final_answer: mRNA vaccines work by delivering a piece of genetic material (mRNA) into the body. This mRNA contains instructions for cells to produce a harmless piece of the virus's protein. Once the cells produce this protein, the immune system recognizes it as foreign and starts building an immune response, including producing antibodies. This prepares the body to fight off the actual virus if exposed in the future.
